title: 429 spikes on bursty batch workloads
summary: Several customers saw bursts of HTTP 429 responses when batch-style jobs suddenly increased concurrency.
symptoms: 429 responses clustered within 1-3 minute bursts
Interactive traffic was mostly unaffected
Retries without jitter caused repeated throttling
root_cause: A concurrency protection limit was reached during synchronized bursts. Several client retry loops retried immediately, amplifying the spike.
resolution: Support recommended exponential backoff with jitter and helped affected customers smooth concurrency. Capacity policy was adjusted for the affected pool.
support_notes: First check whether 429s correlate with a sudden concurrency increase. Ask for retry behavior and whether requests are bursty or steady.

title: High TTFT after large prompt rollout
summary: A customer reported a sharp increase in time-to-first-token after shipping much larger system prompts.
symptoms: TTFT increased while inter-token latency remained stable
Prompt lengths roughly tripled
Generation lengths did not materially change
root_cause: The workload became prefill-heavy. Larger uncached prompts increased prefill compute and delayed first-token delivery.
resolution: The customer reduced repeated prompt content and enabled prompt-prefix reuse where applicable.
support_notes: Separate TTFT from decode speed. Inspect prompt length and repeated prefixes before assuming a general serving regression.

title: Streaming pauses during slow client consumption
summary: Users described streaming responses as 'stalling' even though model generation remained healthy.
symptoms: Server-side generation metrics looked normal
Pauses were more common on mobile and constrained networks
Disconnects sometimes occurred after long pauses
root_cause: Client-side consumption was slower than token production, creating backpressure between the API stream and downstream application.
resolution: The customer fixed stream consumption and cancellation handling and reduced unnecessary buffering.
support_notes: Check whether the stall is model-side or downstream. Compare server generation timing with client receive timing.

title: Unexpected output format broke downstream parser
summary: An extraction workflow occasionally returned valid prose instead of the JSON shape expected by the application.
symptoms: Most requests succeeded
Failures appeared as JSON parse errors
Prompt-only formatting instructions were used
root_cause: The application relied on natural-language formatting instructions rather than schema-constrained structured output.
resolution: The workflow moved to schema-constrained structured outputs and added validation before downstream use.
support_notes: When a parser assumes a contract, prefer structured outputs and validate the response rather than relying on prompt wording alone.

title: Retrieval assistant cites irrelevant policy document
summary: A RAG assistant produced fluent answers grounded in a semantically related but wrong policy version.
symptoms: Answer sounded plausible
Citation pointed to an obsolete policy
Top retrieved chunks shared vocabulary with the query
root_cause: Retrieval did not filter by document version and the reranking stage lacked metadata awareness.
resolution: The customer added version metadata filtering before reranking and required answers to surface source identifiers.
support_notes: Retrieval quality is not just embedding similarity. Check metadata filters, reranking, and whether the answer exposes its evidence.

title: Tool-calling agent loops on the same action
summary: An agent repeatedly called the same search tool with near-identical arguments and failed to converge.
symptoms: Repeated tool calls with minimal query changes
Latency and token usage increased rapidly
Final answer was sometimes never produced
root_cause: The agent loop had no explicit termination policy, no duplicate-call guard, and weak tool-result summarization.
resolution: The customer capped tool steps, rejected duplicate calls, and supplied concise tool results back to the model.
support_notes: For agent loops, inspect step limits, duplicate actions, tool-result size, and explicit conditions for returning a final answer.

title: Latency regression after model switch
summary: A team switched to a larger model and reported worse end-to-end latency despite similar request volume.
symptoms: Both TTFT and generation time increased
Prompt sizes stayed approximately constant
The new model generated somewhat longer answers
root_cause: The chosen model had a materially different serving profile and the application did not adjust max output length or model choice by task complexity.
resolution: The customer introduced simple model routing and tighter output limits for lightweight requests.
support_notes: Do not treat all latency regressions as infrastructure incidents. Compare model, prompt, output length, and workload mix.

title: Repeated system prompt not benefiting from cache
summary: A customer expected repeated prompts to be cheap and fast but saw little improvement across requests.
symptoms: Large common system instructions appeared on every request
Small request-to-request differences occurred near the beginning of the prompt
Cache hit behavior was lower than expected
root_cause: Dynamic content was inserted before the reusable prefix, preventing effective prefix reuse.
resolution: The prompt was reorganized so stable instructions formed the shared prefix and dynamic content appeared later.
support_notes: For prefix-cache issues, inspect exactly where dynamic tokens first diverge, not just whether the prompts look mostly identical.

title: Support bot answers confidently without evidence
summary: A support assistant answered questions that were not covered by its knowledge base instead of acknowledging missing evidence.
symptoms: Answers were fluent but unsupported
No retrieval result threshold existed
The UI did not distinguish sourced and unsourced claims
root_cause: The application always forced an answer and lacked an evidence threshold or abstention behavior.
resolution: The team added an insufficient-evidence path and required the model to ground factual answers in retrieved source IDs.
support_notes: A trustworthy RAG product needs a graceful 'I don't have enough evidence' behavior.

title: Agent slows down after verbose tool results
summary: An internal research agent became slower and more expensive as a session progressed.
symptoms: Each tool response injected full raw documents
Context size grew every step
Later model calls were slower and more expensive
root_cause: Tool results were passed back verbatim instead of being scoped to the fields needed for the next decision.
resolution: The team returned compact structured tool results and fetched full document content only when needed.
support_notes: Keep tool results small. Return identifiers and relevant snippets first; fetch detail on demand.

title: Citations mismatch after answer regeneration
summary: A document assistant sometimes showed citations that no longer matched claims after the final answer was regenerated.
symptoms: Source list was generated in an earlier step
Final prose was regenerated separately
Some claims had no corresponding evidence
root_cause: Citation selection and answer generation were decoupled without a final grounding check.
resolution: The response schema was changed so claims and source IDs were generated together and validated against retrieved IDs.
support_notes: Bind claims to source identifiers in the same structured response, or run a final evidence-validation pass.

title: Search tool returns too many low-value results
summary: An agent's search tool regularly returned 20 documents, overwhelming the model with partially relevant context.
symptoms: Large tool payloads
Answers mixed multiple unrelated incidents
Higher latency with worse grounding
root_cause: The search tool optimized recall without controlling result count or relevance threshold.
resolution: The team reduced default top-k, added score thresholds, and allowed the agent to refine the query when evidence was weak.
support_notes: More context is not automatically better. Prefer a small relevant evidence set and let the agent search again if needed.
